# 架构蓝图设计与演化

负责仓库级系统设计。正式交付经用户确认、内部一致且足以指导研发的 Blueprint，以及适用的架构决定和验证依据。只讨论按[需求与架构讨论](../../sdd/references/sdd-repository-governance.md#需求与架构讨论)交付。专项评估按约定提供方案、证据及待决项。

## 触发与依据

用户明确发起本轮架构任务时使用，由本 Skill 组织阶段内工作。其他阶段发现的信号作为架构输入。

| 场景 | 本轮关注点 |
| --- | --- |
| 新项目建立整体架构 | 从已确认产品目标、范围和约束确定系统边界及关键决定 |
| 已有仓库补建蓝图 | 区分可取证的现状、已确认的设计和候选目标设计 |
| 规模、性能、可靠性、部署形态或技术生命周期变化 | 比较演化路径及对系统约束的影响 |
| 需求触及模块职责、依赖方向、状态权威或关键契约 | 依据已确认需求设计受影响的跨模块关系与约束 |
| 运行、测试或审查提出系统性风险 | 从证据定位风险、影响与决定需求 |
| 架构迁移或退役 | 确定目标、过渡状态、兼容、数据处置和恢复条件 |

从项目索引定位已有 Blueprint、契约、ADR、Spec 和可用证据，按问题读取适用部分。以实际版本和观测条件标注实现、部署和运行事实。缺少决策依据时提出待决问题。

需要用户确认时，技能 Agent 将拟决定内容及证据交 Main，并按用户反馈续做。

## 本轮闭环

分析深度由设计问题及风险决定，不以交付模板的字段逐项限制分析，也不将分析涉及的所有内容转化为交付项。

1. 按[意图对齐](../../sdd/references/visual-confirmation.md#意图对齐)提出本轮架构问题、目标、范围、交付物和完成条件，确认其中新增或变化的内容。沿用已确认的产品需求及设计。保留相关现状证据、约束、缺项和受影响决定。待定的业务依据交回 Main，受影响的设计保持候选。
2. 比较可行方案及适用条件。按影响设计系统边界、模块职责、依赖方向、状态权威与关键不变量，明确关键交互、契约、异常传播和恢复责任。涉及运行时，明确部署拓扑、环境隔离、存储与数据边界、可靠性及可观测性。涉及演化时，说明受影响的模块和调用方、兼容约束、过渡状态、切换与回退条件。把成本、性能、可靠性等取舍对应到已确认的目标。
3. 用现有证据或相称的可行性实验验证影响决策的关键假设。明确观察点、通过判据、条件、实际结果与局限。实验超出已有授权时先确认所需授权，包括外部资源、费用、真实数据或不可逆影响。实验代码和配置按[工程资产边界](../../sdd/references/sdd-repository-governance.md#工程资产边界)隔离，实际结果按需引用 [Test Report](../../sdd/assets/test_report_template.md)。证据推翻关键假设时回到方案比较，修订并验证受影响的部分。
4. 按完整设计问题或决策批次提交方案及证据供用户确认，覆盖新增或变化的模块边界、状态权威、依赖方向、关键选型及成本、可靠性、性能等实质取舍。证据与已确认决定或业务依据与技术约束出现实质冲突时，重新确认受影响决定。常规调查、授权内实验、表达形式、文档归并和一致性修正持续执行。待决事项只影响相关决定及其依赖。
5. 获授权后按[文档写入规则](../../sdd/references/document-writing.md)原位归并已确认内容。沿用项目 Blueprint，按 [Blueprint 模板](../../sdd/assets/blueprint_template.md)规定的结构与内容归并已确认的高层设计结论。项目已有 ADR、[Technical Research and Selection Report](../../sdd/assets/research_template.md)、[Scenario Sequence](../../sdd/assets/sequence_template.md)、[Interface Contract](../../sdd/assets/contract_template.md) 及验证报告按本轮约定和适用产物要求维护；参考或分析这些内容不自动要求新增对应文档。核对职责、依赖、状态权威、契约、过渡状态及直接引用，按需同步索引，保留稳定编号。写后检查针对设计内部一致性。

按设计问题迭代，简单任务可合并步骤。回执给出已确认结论、权威章节、关键验证及证据、剩余风险。完成判断依据本轮约定、蓝图模板及适用的写后检查，不因采用某种分析方法而额外要求对应报告或完整分析记录。必要决定已确认、约定验证完成且权威正文已归并并通过一致性检查后，报告正式交付完成。仍待决或未验证的事项注明影响和恢复条件，按受影响范围报告完成状态。

## 执行安排与阶段边界

本 Skill 按[委派与独立性](../../sdd/references/delegation.md#委派与独立性)选择执行者，回收实际结果用于本轮架构判断。

| 何时安排 | 专业工作及给定依据 | 回收结果 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 需要系统性设计或技术取舍 | 架构分析与设计；给定待决问题、已确认约束、影响范围和现状证据 | 可归并方案、取舍依据、受影响决定和待决项 |
| 关键假设需要实验代码 | 限定实验目标、写入范围、观察点、通过判据和隔离条件 | 实验入口、实际改动、环境、版本、结果和限制 |
| 设计判断需要运行或环境证据 | 给定目标环境、版本、只读取证范围和观察点 | 可追溯的部署、依赖或运行事实及覆盖缺口 |
| 需要独立核对正式文档的一致性 | 按[文档交接](../../sdd/references/delegation.md#文档交接)指定只读范围、权威条款与疑点 | 冲突或引用问题、证据和建议，由获授权的写入者处理 |

业务需求定义、正式产品代码改造、实际架构遵循 Review、部署运行操作由 Main 按[阶段授权与推进](../../sdd/references/sdd-repository-governance.md#阶段授权与推进)安排。将相关问题、影响、依据和接续条件随回执交回 Main。

## Code Review Rules

用户明确要求生成或更新 Code Review Rules 时，读取[目标仓库的 Code Review Rules](sdd-repository-governance.md#目标仓库的-code-review-rules)的决策边界，按默认落点或项目映射定位正文。依据已确认的 Blueprint、契约与实际运行路径选用[架构规范](architecture-rules.md)中的适用约束，按 [Code Review Rules](../assets/code-review-rules_template.md)写成针对本项目入口和职责的可检查规则。同义规则原位归并，保留稳定标识；逐项核对受影响条款，移除明确撤销的约束。缺乏设计依据的归属或冲突列为待决。仅维护规则内容，执行证据归 Review。
# Blueprint — Product and Architecture

> Record confirmed objectives. Refer to Status or Tasks for implementation progress and to Test Reports for verification results and evidence. Maintain one Blueprint for the entire product. It defines high-level use cases, key experiences, and acceptance dimensions. Refer to the relevant Spec for detailed FRs and ACs and to the owning Interface Contract for mechanisms. Keep each detail in its authoritative document.

Link the product requirement that drives a decision beside the corresponding responsibility or invariant. Link the relevant Scenario Sequence when ordering, concurrency, or failure affects the user experience.

## 1. Product Goals and Scope

Describe the target users, their problem, the value, and what is included, optional, or excluded. Capture key experiences in the use cases and BDD scenarios below. Keep essential details and link the relevant PUCs and PACs.

## 2. Clients and Operating Conditions

| Environment ID | Client and usage context | Required operating conditions | Capability differences and support scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| PENV-01 | <Device and browser or app> | <Confirmed network, permission, and version requirements> | <Product commitments and limitations> |

Describe client support commitments separately from deployment locations. Record version coverage in acceptance evidence and collect open questions in section 8.

## 3. Product Use Cases

Organize product-wide use cases by user goal. Use a Mermaid `flowchart` to show actors, the system boundary, goals, and relevant relationships. Use a `subgraph` for the system boundary, with use cases inside and actors outside. Connect related elements. Use `include`, `extend`, or generalization only when the relationship matches its UML semantics.

| Use case ID | Actor, goal, and key experience | Applicable environment and detailed requirements |
|---|---|---|
| PUC-01 | <Confirmed user goal> | <PENV or relevant Spec section> |

## 4. High-Level Acceptance Scenarios and Dimensions

Use Given–When–Then to describe representative scenarios and acceptance dimensions. A table or Gherkin is sufficient. An automation framework is optional.

| ID / Use case | Given | When | Then — High-level expectation and acceptance dimension |
|---|---|---|---|
| PAC-01 / PUC-01 | <Specific precondition> | <Specific trigger> | <High-level expectation and acceptance dimension. Link the Spec AC for the detailed criteria.> |

Cover key experiences, success, edge cases, failure, cancellation, and recovery according to risk. Describe operations separately when their preconditions, triggers, or rules differ. Parameterize only when the expected behavior follows the same logic. Give distinct triggers, cancellations, and failures their own expected outcomes. Describe an actual scenario for each entry and use links to support it. When splitting a scenario, preserve traceability to the original PAC and retain existing FR and AC identifiers.

Use PACs for product quality dimensions. Refer to Spec ACs for specific conditions, thresholds, timing boundaries, units, statistical definitions, and evidence types. Link available acceptance evidence for the actual integrated version and agreed environment. Follow the [Testing Scope Constraints](../references/sdd-repository-governance.md#testing-scope-constraints).

## 5. Deployment and Runtime Boundaries

Use a deployment view to describe the project's confirmed deployment units and runtime boundaries. A Mermaid flowchart can depict this view. A Mermaid flowchart is a deployment view expressed outside UML syntax. Identify separate processes only when the confirmed deployment design calls for them. Link existing engineering documentation for source directories and build entry points.

Record confirmed design strategies, rationale, costs, and applicable conditions. Link the relevant PUCs and PACs, and refer to the Spec for product quality criteria.

## 6. Components and Responsibilities

Use a component diagram to show responsibilities, I/O, interfaces, allowed and prohibited dependencies, key concepts, and their relationships and boundaries. Record who produces and consumes each concept and who owns authoritative data. Define essential terms briefly. Add a separate relationship diagram only if it conveys information absent from the component diagram and overall sequence.

| Component | Responsibilities, state ownership, and prohibited interactions | Interface Contract |
|---|---|---|
| <Confirmed component> | <Requester, decision maker, writer, side-effect executor, authoritative state owner, and evidence of completion> | <Owning Interface Contract section> |

Add a compact data table when useful to explain sources, authority, permitted reads and writes, and lifecycle. Preserve these distinctions when combining tables. Put detailed payloads, authorization, cancellation, results, and failure semantics in the owning Interface Contract.

## 7. Architecture Invariants

| ID | Constraint | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| <Stable ARC identifier> | <Rule that holds during normal operation, failure, concurrency, cancellation, and recovery> | <Responsibility or Interface Contract reference> |

Record project invariants the user has confirmed. Preserve stable identifiers, applicability conditions, and the strength of each constraint. Refer to section 6 for existing responsibility lists. List unconfirmed environments, frameworks, and strategies as open questions. Use the confirmed design and this template as the basis. Reading the architecture rules and adding rule mappings are outside this step.

## 8. Key Interactions and Open Questions

| Product scenario | Interface Contract / Scenario Sequence |
|---|---|
| <PUC or PAC and interaction goal> | <Links to public interfaces and key interactions> |

Use the index to link responsibilities and detailed flows. Use the [Scenario Sequence template](sequence_template.md) to describe normal ordering, parallelism, races, cancellation, late results, unknown outcomes, and recovery across public interfaces. Keep internal algorithms outside this view. Record interface and failure semantics in the [Interface Contract](contract_template.md). Use activity diagrams for complex branches, joins, or data processing, distinguishing control flow from object flow. Include state or ER diagrams when useful. Internal class diagrams are optional.

| Open question | Source, impact, and decision needed |
|---|---|
| <Material gap> | <Related clause or Task> |

Collect open questions here and link any authoritative list already maintained in a Task. Keep uncertain or infeasible items open. Fill sections as applicable. Record governance activity and check evidence in the Task.

## Architecture Modeling and Assessment

Sections 1–4 cover product goals and acceptance dimensions. Section 5 covers runtime boundaries and trade-offs. Sections 6–7 cover concepts, responsibilities, and invariants. Section 8 indexes key interactions and open questions. Combine sections or link existing documents to suit the project. The project confirms module count, architectural planes, directory layout, technical patterns, and deployment. Record missing decisions as open questions.

Follow the [Repository Governance](../references/sdd-repository-governance.md#authoritative-documents) for document ownership and the [Document Writing Rules](../references/document-writing.md) when consolidating clauses or verifying a migration.
# Scenario Sequence

> Show key interactions among modules, public interfaces, and external actors. Keep internal classes, private methods, and algorithm steps outside this view. Use the project index to find the authoritative location. A module can share a Scenario Sequence with other modules.

## Key Scenarios

| Scenario | Requirement basis | Modules and external actors | Interface Contract |

## 委派与独立性

调度方按任务所需能力和[最小交接](#最小交接)显式委派，按输入输出契约选择执行者。受托角色按[角色独立执行](#角色独立执行)处理工单。

对应角色不可用时，选用合格替代或由具备能力的调度方按同一契约在其职责范围内承接。确实缺少必要能力时记录缺口及恢复条件。明确共享文件归属，保留其他执行者的修改。有实际收益且互不干扰的工作可并行。复验及复核优先复用原执行者。项目或用户对独立审查、验收有要求时，核对实际执行者是否独立。

以 `collaboration.spawn_agent` 启动专业角色也使用 `fork_turns="none"` 和 `message`。用户指定的模型和推理强度优先。角色配置不固定推理强度，其余由调度方按子任务复杂度选择，启动接口支持时显式传入。启动接口不能设置模型或强度时按实际配置报告。

### 角色独立执行

角色可直接受理合格工单，在授权内使用适用的项目正文、共享规则、模板和工具完成本职产物及写后检查。角色禁止加载工作流 Skill、依赖其内部规则或委派其他角色。按[任务回执](task-receipt.md)向任务调用者交付结果、证据、缺口和接续条件。

## 实施交接

调度方按[最小交接](#最小交接)安排已授权的调查或准备，在工单就绪、实施获授权且阶段确认已满足时安排实施。已有需求、缺陷和 Review 工单直接引用可执行的[验收计划与方案](sdd-repository-governance.md#验收计划与方案)。已确认的架构变更或获授权的探索可按各自目标、范围、完成条件和必要依据交办。只规格、只评估、只审查和只验收按用户限定终点交付。

执行者发现必要依据、判据或授权缺失时，按[任务回执](task-receipt.md)先交任务调用者，写明缺项、影响和恢复条件。阶段内由技能 Agent 在职责与授权范围内补齐并接续原工单。涉及跨阶段、需用户决定或超出授权时，由技能 Agent 交 Main 协调。技能未覆盖的工单由直接受理的 Main 处理。受影响项及其依赖按[阶段授权与推进](sdd-repository-governance.md#阶段授权与推进)暂停，其余已就绪且获授权的工作继续。

# 文档校验 CLI

统一入口为项目内 `.agents/skills/sdd-workflow/sdd/scripts/doc_check.py`，Python 3.11+，仅依赖标准库，只读、不访问网络、不更新状态或 Gate。写入者执行机械检查并完成语义核对。

## 使用

从项目根目录执行，显式传入本次修改和直接受影响的文件或目录：

```powershell
python -B .agents/skills/sdd-workflow/sdd/scripts/doc_check.py --root . specs/payment/spec.md docs/blueprint.md
python -B .agents/skills/sdd-workflow/sdd/scripts/doc_check.py --root . --format json docs/test-reports
```

路径相对 `--root` 解析，也可传入根目录内的绝对路径。目录递归选择 `.md`，排除 `.git`、`.build`、`node_modules`、`.venv`、`__pycache__`；文件去重。范围为空、文件不存在、非 Markdown 文件或路径越出根目录均报错。直接检查的文件和目录必须位于根目录内。运行项目已接入的 `.agents/skills/sdd-workflow/sdd/scripts/doc_check.py` 时，允许解析经该共享入口指向同一共享根内的 Markdown。核对托管导航可运行 `python -B .agents/skills/sdd-workflow/sdd/scripts/doc_check.py --root . AGENTS.md`。链接检查只核对存在性及锚点；反向引用按本次变更显式纳入。

文本结果逐项输出 `文件:行号: 级别 规则码: 问题`。JSON 包含 `schema_version`、`scope=mechanical_only`、`files`、`diagnostics`、`errors` 和 `warnings`。行号从 1 开始，文件诊断使用项目相对路径；根目录外的输入显示实际路径。

退出码：`0` 表示无机械错误，仍可能有警告；`1` 表示存在错误，或使用 `--strict` 时存在警告；`2` 表示命令参数错误。默认不启用 strict，不将需要人工判断的警告自动变成项目门禁。

## 按章节读取

`--read` 接受一个或多个 `文件#标题锚点`。输出该标题及其正文，到下一个标题为止。标题前的独立 `<a id="...">` 或 `<a name="...">` 空锚点可作为同一章节的别名。需要选取表格行时追加 `:首列值`，多行用逗号分隔。保留该节正文、表头和匹配行。路径与锚点超出支持范围或选定行不存在时返回错误，供调用者核对选择器。读取模式不执行文档检查。

## 检查范围

| 规则 | 机械检查 | 默认级别 |
|---|---|---|
| DOC000 | 输入缺失、越界、类型错误或未选择任何 Markdown | 错误 |
| DOC001 | 无法读取 UTF-8、非法编码或 NUL；允许 UTF-8 BOM 和 CRLF | 错误 |
| DOC002 | 顶层反引号／波浪线代码围栏或文件头 YAML 未闭合 | 错误 |
| DOC003 | ATX／Setext 标题层级跳跃；不强制首标题 H1 | 警告 |
| DOC004 | 具有标准分隔行的管道表格列数不一致；转义及行内代码中的竖线不计列 | 错误 |
| DOC005 | 同一文件中的 FR／AC／ARC／PUC／PAC／PENV 或 T001 类编号重复声明 | 错误 |
| DOC006 | 已识别单行链接的目标不合法或不在支持的目标语法内 | 错误 |
| DOC007 | 本地目标不存在或越出根目录 | 错误 |
| DOC008 | 本地 Markdown 目标不存在对应标题锚点或显式 HTML id/name | 错误 |
| DOC009 | 全式／折叠式引用链接缺少定义，或引用标签重复定义 | 错误 |
| DOC010 | 模板路径占位符或非 Markdown 文件的 fragment 未检查 | 警告 |

编号声明限于列表或标题起始的 `FR-001:` / `T001：` 形式，以及首列表头为 `ID` 的定义表首列；含 `Result`、`Evidence`、`Snapshot` 的结果表不作为声明。正文提及编号不视为声明；跨文档引用是否对应同一语义、编号是否在迁移中稳定由 Agent 核对。

 - ARC-001 The API authenticates clients, the Order Service owns order state, and the repository commits changes on behalf of the service. The API remains the public response boundary. See the [create contract](create-contract.md) and the [create sequence](create-sequence.md).
+
+The Order Service writes order state and one OrderCreated outbox record through the repository in the same storage transaction. The dispatcher reads only committed outbox records, publishes asynchronously, and retries by event ID. The dispatcher depends on committed storage state; the API response does not depend on dispatch completion. Order state remains authoritative in storage under the Order Service's ownership.
+
+## Architecture invariants
+
+- ARC-002 Order state and its OrderCreated outbox record commit atomically. Neither write is visible to the dispatcher before a successful commit. A transaction failure rolls back both writes and the API returns 503, with no success response or created event. Once the transaction is durable, the API may return 201 with the order identifier while dispatch remains pending; event delivery is not a prerequisite. The dispatcher publishes committed records asynchronously and retries by event ID. This preserves [CON-001](create-contract.md) and is realized in [SCN-001](create-sequence.md#create-order), based on the [confirmed design decision](decision.md).
*** Update File: /tmp/sdd-review-execution-t7u939o0/architecture_design-ykcanutr/prepared/project/docs/create-sequence.md
@@
-- SCN-001 The API authenticates the caller, validates input and calls the Order Service. The Order Service persists the order. The API returns the identifier after persistence.
+- SCN-001 The API authenticates the caller, validates input and calls the Order Service. The Order Service persists the order and one OrderCreated outbox record in the same storage transaction through the repository. A successful commit makes the records visible to the dispatcher and permits the API to return 201 with the order identifier. The dispatcher publishes asynchronously and retries by event ID. A transaction failure rolls back both writes and returns 503 without a success response or created event.
+
+Participants are the caller, API, Order Service, repository, transactional storage, dispatcher, and event consumers. This sequence follows [ARC-001 and ARC-002](blueprint.md) and preserves the public response and event semantics in [CON-001](create-contract.md).
+
+```mermaid
+sequenceDiagram
+    actor Caller
+    participant API
+    participant Service as Order Service
+    participant Repository
+    participant Storage as Transactional storage
+    participant Dispatcher
+    participant Consumer as Event consumers
+
+    Caller->>API: POST /orders
+    Note over API: Authenticate caller and validate input
+    API->>Service: Create order
+    Service->>Repository: Persist order and one OrderCreated outbox record atomically
+    Repository->>Storage: Write both records in one transaction
+    Note over Storage,Dispatcher: Neither write is visible to dispatcher before commit
+    alt Transaction commits successfully
+        Storage-->>Repository: Both records committed and durable
+        Repository-->>Service: Persistence succeeded, order identifier
+        par API response after durability
+            Service-->>API: Order identifier
+            API-->>Caller: 201 with order identifier
+        and Asynchronous dispatch after commit
+            Dispatcher->>Storage: Read committed outbox records
+            Storage-->>Dispatcher: OrderCreated record with event ID
+            Dispatcher->>Consumer: Publish OrderCreated asynchronously
+            Note over Dispatcher,Consumer: On publication failure, retry by the same event ID
+        end
+    else Transaction fails
+        Storage-->>Repository: Failure; both writes rolled back
+        Repository-->>Service: Persistence failed
+        Service-->>API: Persistence failed
+        API-->>Caller: 503
+        Note over Storage,Consumer: No committed outbox record, no created event
+    end
+```
+
+The two success branches require a successful commit but do not require an ordering between the 201 response and publication. Dispatch may remain pending when 201 is returned. Publication failure leaves the committed order and outbox record durable for dispatcher retries by event ID; it does not cause the transaction-failure response. The dispatcher never publishes records from a failed transaction. The diagram specifies the confirmed design, not evidence of runtime implementation.
*** End Patch"));
